A_target.statement: There is no [[Definition:Retraction (Topology)|retraction]] $r: \Bbb D^2 \to \Bbb S^1$ of the closed disk onto its boundary circle.

B_source.statement: $\map {\pi_1} {\Bbb S^1} \cong \Z$, $\map {\pi_1} {\Bbb D^2}$ is [[Definition:Trivial Group|trivial]], and $\pi_1$ is a [[Definition:Functor|functor]]: $\paren {g \circ f}_* = g_* \circ f_*$ and $\paren {\operatorname {id} }_* = \operatorname {id}$.

derived.the induced homomorphisms: a factorization of the identity of Z through the trivial group

object_map.reformulation: Apply the fundamental group functor to the equation r composed with inclusion equals identity.

validity_conditions: Functoriality is what turns the topological identity into an algebraic one.
The same argument with higher homology groups gives the statement in all dimensions.
proof_plan: {{AimForCont}} $r$ is a retraction, so $r \circ i = \operatorname {id}_{\Bbb S^1}$, where $i: \Bbb S^1 \to \Bbb D^2$ is the inclusion.
But $i_*$ maps into the trivial group $\map {\pi_1} {\Bbb D^2}$, so $r_* \circ i_* = 0$, while $\operatorname {id}_\Z \ne 0$.
